summary: Godefroy de Blonay was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (diplôme ~1891–1894). He served as Privatdozent of Indology at the University of Neuchâtel from 1911 to 1929.

Godfrey Edward Phillips worked in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology, earning an M.A. from Mansfield College. He served as Professor at United Theological College, Bangalore (1910), Foreign Secretary for the London Missionary Society (1926–1935), and Professor at Kingsmead College (1926–1944).

Gokulmuthu Narayanaswamy is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at IIT Madras, IISc, Annamalai University, and IIT Kharagpur (Ph.D. 2020). He worked at Synergy Infotech (1997–2004), Sonim Technologies (2004–2016), and Itron (2016).

Gombojab Tsybikov was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksey Pozdneev, later teaching at the Eastern Institute, Far Eastern Federal University, and Irkutsk State University.

Gopal Lal Meena is an Indologist who taught Shagun Sinha. His career includes posts as Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Professor emeritus at the University of Delhi, both attested in 2026.
Gopikamohan Bhattacharya worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Erich Frauwallner. He held an attested post at Kurukshetra University in 1977.

Gopinath Kaviraj was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar educated at University Maharani College and University of Allahabad under Arthur Venis, Madhusudan Ojha, and Shashadhar Tarkachuramani. He served as librarian, Principal, and Head of Yoga-Tantra at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Gordon Charles Roadarmel worked in Indology, studying at the College of Wooster, Chicago Theological Seminary, University of Allahabad, and UC Berkeley (Ph.D. ~1969). He taught Hindi at the University of Chicago (1963–1965) and was Assistant Professor at UC Berkeley (~1969–1972).

Gordon Dester Kaufman was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Bethel College, Northwestern, and Yale (Ph.D. ~1955). He held posts at Pomona College, Vanderbilt University, and Harvard University as Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity (1963).

Gordon H. Fairbanks was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Alberta and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (Ph.D. ~1948). His academic posts included Cornell University (1945–1970) and Professor of Linguistics at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1970).

Gordon Hannington Luce was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and linguistics. Educated at Emmanuel College, Cambridge (~1908–1911), he spent his career as a Professor at the University of Rangoon (~1912–1964).

Gordon Johnson is a historian and Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He held fellowships at Trinity and Selwyn College, served as President of Wolfson College (1993–2010), Cambridge Deputy Vice-Chancellor (1974–2010), and President of the Royal Asiatic Society (2015–2018).

Gordon Matthews worked in Indology and linguistics after earning degrees at Merton College and Mansfield College. He served as Professor of English and Vice-Principal at Madras Christian College (~1913–1939) and Lecturer in Tamil at SOAS University of London (1939).

Gore Ouseley worked in the fields of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts with the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (~1810–1815) and served as Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1844).

Gottfried Bernhardy was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. Educated at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1817–1822), he held a post at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from ~1829 to 1875.

Gottfried Ernst Groddeck was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology who studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen (~1782–1786). He held a post at Vilnius University (Imperial University of Vilna) from ~1803 to 1824.
Gottfried Hartmann Weigle was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Tübingen (~1834–1838). In 1838, he became a missionary for the Basel Mission.

Gottfried Hermann was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Leipzig and University of Jena. He spent his career at the University of Leipzig, serving as extraordinary professor of philosophy (1798) and director of the philological seminar (1803–1848).
Gottfried Kinkel was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Bonn (~1831–1834). He held academic posts at the University of Bonn (~1837–1848) and at ETH Zurich (~1866–1882).
Gottlieb L. Schaenzlin was an Indology scholar who earned an M.A. from Johns Hopkins University (~1920–1921). In 1914, he served as Principal of the Collins Institute.
